statement: The second hand of a clock goes once round the face every minute. Which of these is closest to the number of times it goes round in one week?

choices.misconception: I counted the hours in a week, 168, instead of the minutes.
I counted the minutes in one day, 1440, and forgot to multiply by 7 days.
I worked out the seconds in one day, $60 \times 60 \times 24$, which is 86,400.
I counted the seconds in a week, about 600,000, instead of full turns.

hints: Count the minutes in a week: minutes in an hour, hours in a day, days in a week. Round each step to make the multiplying easy.
There are $24 \times 60 = 1440$ minutes in a day.

solutions.reliable: Turns in a week = minutes in a week $= 60 \times 24 \times 7 = 1440 \times 7 = 10{,}080$, which is closest to 10,000. The transferable idea: estimate by counting the right unit, then compare orders of magnitude.
solutions.elegant: Round: about 1500 minutes a day, times 7 is about 10,000. The choices are far apart, so rough rounding is enough.

whyOnTest: Order-of-magnitude estimation: choose the right unit, round sensibly, and the far-apart choices do the rest.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
